hints: Focus on the shape and bonding around each carbon in ethene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, not just the double bond itself.
Each carbon joins to two H atoms and one C atom by sigma bonds, giving three sigma regions and one leftover p orbital, so think what hybridisation that means.
Now count every single bond plus the sigma part of the double bond as sigma, and remember the second part of the double bond is the only pi bond.
walkthrough:
**Draw out the structure of ethene**

Think of ethene as $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$. It is flat with a C=C double bond in the middle and two C-H bonds on each carbon.

$$\text{H} - \overset{\text{H}}{\underset{}{\text{C}}} = \overset{\text{H}}{\underset{}{\text{C}}} - \text{H}$$

**Find the hybridisation of each carbon**

Each carbon makes 3 sigma connections (2 to H, 1 to C) and has no lone pairs. That is 3 electron regions, which is trigonal planar.

Three regions means one s and two p orbitals mix, so the carbon is $\text{sp}^2$ hybridised, leaving one unhybridised p orbital for pi bonding.

**Count the overall sigma and pi bonds**

Every single bond is one $\sigma$ bond, so the four C-H bonds give 4 $\sigma$. The C=C double bond is made of one $\sigma$ plus one $\pi$.

$$\text{Total } \sigma = 4 + 1 = 5, \quad \text{Total } \pi = 1$$

**Match to the row**

$\text{sp}^2$ with 5 $\sigma$ bonds and 1 $\pi$ bond fits perfectly. That is the complete description for one molecule.

options.A: Hybridisation is correct as sp2, but the bond count is short by one. Students often count only the four C-H sigma bonds and forget the C-C sigma bond that is also part of the C=C double bond.
options.B: This is correct. Each carbon is sp2 with trigonal planar geometry, and the whole $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ molecule has 5 sigma bonds (4 C-H + 1 C-C) plus 1 pi bond from the C=C.
options.C: Both parts are off for ethene. sp3 is for tetrahedral carbons with four sigma regions, like in ethane, not for a double-bonded planar carbon. The 4 sigma count also misses the C-C sigma bond.
options.D: The bond count of 5 sigma and 1 pi is right, but sp3 is wrong. Students sometimes pick sp3 because carbon makes four bonds in total, but in ethene one of those is a pi bond, so only three sigma regions means sp2, not sp3.
